title: Όλυμπος: Αίσιο τέλος στην επιχειρηση διάσωσης 34χρονου τραυματισμένου ορειβάτη
content:
Αίσιο τέλος είχε η επιχείρηση διάσωσης ενός 34χρονου αλλοδαπού, ο οποίος τραυματίστηκε σε δύσβατο σημείο, κοντά στη θέση Σπηλιά Ιθακήσιου στον Όλυμπο, σε υψόμετρο περίπου 1.800 μέτρων.
Για το περιστατικό ενημερώθηκε το Κέντρο Επιχειρήσεων του Πυροσβεστικού Σώματος περίπου στη 1 το μεσημέρι του Σαββάτου 19 Σεπτεμβρίου, έπειτα από κλήση στο 112. Μετά τον άμεσο γεωεντοπισμό του ορειβάτη, κινητοποιήθηκαν 11 πυροσβέστες με τρία πυροσβεστικά οχήματα από τη 2η και την 8η ΕΜΑΚ, καθώς και από την Πυροσβεστική Υπηρεσία Λιτοχώρου.
Οι πυροσβέστες προσέγγισαν τον 34χρονο και, με τη χρήση ορειβατικού εξοπλισμού, τον μετέφεραν σε ασφαλές σημείο, όπου τον παρέλαβε ασθενοφόρο του ΕΚΑΒ.
Η επιχείρηση ολοκληρώθηκε λίγο πριν από τις 10 το βράδυ του Σαββάτου.

title: New Insights on the 17 Haitians Found on the Shores of Santiago de Cuba
content:
The Cuban Red Cross in Santiago de Cuba shared further details this Thursday about the care provided to the 17 Haitian nationals discovered this week on Siboney Beach. The aid included the provision of food and water, psychological support, and a revised account of the intended destination of their vessel.
According to a Facebook post by the organization, the migrants had spent several days at sea before reaching Cuban shores, with their boat originally setting sail for Jamaica.
This updated information contrasts with the initial reports following their arrival, which suggested the group had departed Haiti aiming for the United States but ended up in Santiago de Cuba due to adverse weather conditions altering their course.
The Red Cross also noted that it activated its humanitarian response protocols, deploying aid and relief personnel in collaboration with local authorities.
Medical and paramedical staff from Public Health, along with Red Cross members, assessed the 17 individuals. The organization reported that no health risks or concerning symptoms were detected.
Hygiene and epidemiology experts implemented necessary health checks, while the new arrivals were provided with hydration and nourishment, considering the extended period they had been at sea under inadequate conditions.
Furthermore, the migrants received emotional support and initial psychological assistance following their arduous journey.
Focusing on Vulnerable Individuals
The care efforts particularly emphasized the woman, the young girl, and the boy within the group, as stated by the Red Cross, which confirmed ongoing emotional support and active listening as part of their intervention.
The group consists of 14 men, one woman, one girl, and one boy. Initially, it was reported that they arrived on Siboney Beach after drifting for about a week and were found by medical personnel to be in seemingly good health.
Initial reports also mentioned that Immigration and Foreigners' specialists were responsible for identifying the migrants, while Ministry of the Interior personnel took part in security measures and government representatives handled logistical issues.
Frequently Asked Questions about the Haitian Migrants in Santiago de Cuba
What was the original destination of the Haitian migrants' vessel?
The vessel was initially headed to Jamaica, as revealed by the Cuban Red Cross.
What kind of assistance did the migrants receive in Cuba?
The migrants received food, water, medical evaluations, psychological support, and emotional assistance from the Cuban Red Cross and local health authorities.

title: She pays $96 a month to live in Yellowstone National Park: 'Being here has changed my life'
content:
This story is part of CNBC Make It's Millennial Money series, which details how people around the world earn, spend and save their money.
Zoe De La Paz shares a bedroom with a woman she met just a few months ago. She doesn't have a car and hitchhikes when she needs a ride into town. She occasionally wakes up at 3 a.m. to the siren-like sound of an elk bugle, what she refers to as a "nightmare alarm clock." She's also living what she considers a dream life and working a job she truly loves.
De La Paz, 26, lives in Mammoth Village in Yellowstone National Park, where she works as a seamstress for the uniform department of Xanterra Parks & Resorts, a concessionaire that operates hotels, lodges, restaurants and other businesses in the national park.
Until recently, De La Paz was splitting an apartment with a roommate in Chicago and earning about $75,000 a year as a mechanical designer for an engineering firm. But she was feeling creatively unfulfilled and was looking for a way out. In 2024 she thought she found one during a trip to visit a friend working at Yellowstone. De La Paz says witnessing the park's natural beauty, plus the freedom her friend had through his seasonal job there, planted the seed for her to quit her 9-to-5 desk job and move there one day.
"It was what made me realize that life was too short and that I was very unhappy at my corporate job," she tells CNBC Make It.
De La Paz, who began sewing as a teen cosplayer, brainstormed ways to get back into creative spaces. She took up odd jobs at Chicago-area music venues on nights and weekends; while catering a The Weeknd concert, she connected with the artist's wardrobe team and was hired to do some costuming work for the tour's backup dancers. From there, De La Paz knew she wanted to make the leap back into her creative passion and saw a possibility of making a full-time career out of it.
In early 2026, she began researching her options for a more hands-on, creative sewing gig and found one while checking for jobs at Yellowstone, as she'd done periodically since her trip. By June, she was headed to the national park for her next chapter.
She now spends her days behind a sewing machine, earning $19.25 an hour, and already has plans to take her sewing career to the next level.
"From a young age, I had been told that work must be work and play must be play, and that there isn't necessarily a world that allows both to coexist with one another," De La Paz says. "I never thought that my hobby could become my career."
Behind the machine
De La Paz starts her workdays by hopping on the 6:45 a.m. employee shuttle to make the 15-minute drive from her dorm in Mammoth Village in Wyoming, on the north side of Yellowstone, just across state lines to her work facilities in Gardiner, Montana.
As a tailor for Xanterra's uniform department, her duties include sewing on patches, fixing snaps and replacing buttons and zippers on uniforms for thousands of concessionaire employees, from housekeepers and security officers to restaurant workers and tour guides.
She works 40 hours per week, on Mondays through Fridays, from roughly 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. with an hour-long lunch break.
The summer season kick-off came with a learning curve, De La Paz says: With hundreds of new employees starting within a few weeks of each other, she and the one other tailor on the team worked tirelessly to make sure all the uniforms were in top shape. Some days involved hemming upwards of 40 pairs of pants, she says, and sewing quickly to meet the same-day turnaround time.
She enjoys helping the park's employees, many of them public-facing, to "work comfortably in their uniform" while looking their best, De La Paz says.
The job has plenty of room to be creative. Beyond mending and tailoring, De La Paz's team works on upcycling projects, like turning old employer-issued backpacks into fanny packs after a clear-backpack policy went into effect in the park.
De La Paz's colleagues have a range of life experiences: Her direct manager is a 73-year-old retired educator who's been working in the park system since 2023; one colleague is a grad school student there for the summer, and another is a former hairstylist who took on the park job to see more of the world.
Despite earning less today than at her desk job in Chicago, "the trade-off is really worth it to me because I get to live in one of the most beautiful places in the world," De La Paz says.
She adds that her living and food costs are lower in the park than back in the city, and says the easy access to nature is priceless. Another employee perk: Visiting friends and family members can stay in a room in the park for just $5 a night.
"Even though the national parks are land for the people to come visit, there is just a geographical distance and then a financial distance for people to be able to come and visit and stay in the park," De La Paz says. "Staying in Yellowstone can be just as expensive as traveling internationally, and I'm really grateful that I get to stay for pennies and dimes, essentially, to live inside of the park."
How she spends her money
Here's how De La Paz spent her money in July 2026.
- Discretionary: $1,162 for gifts, entertainment, household items, pet care
- Food: $742, including her meal stipend and eating off-campus
- Savings and investments: $586
- Rent: $96
- Subscriptions: $34 for The New York Times, Rocket Money and to host her freelancing website
- Phone: $20
De La Paz has $96 deducted from her paycheck every month for her employee lodging, which covers her bed in a dorm room she shares with up to two roommates, as well as Wi-Fi and utilities. Dorm living comes with a communal bathroom, laundry facilities, common areas and social events.
She also has about $359 deducted from her paychecks each month to cover a meal stipend for food at Xanterra's six employee dining rooms. In July, De La Paz spent an additional $383 on food outside of those meals, including trips to restaurants and orders from DoorDash.
De La Paz's food and discretionary spending was higher than usual in July, she says, because it was her birthday. She treated herself a new bag, bought a new sewing machine and hosted several groups of family members and friends, meaning extra expenses on dinners out and activities like cruises around Yellowstone Lake. She also got some early holiday shopping done with an extra-generous employee discount on all of Xanterra's gift shops for two weeks in July.
De La Paz has a cat, Pepperjack, back in Chicago and pays her former roommate $200 per month to help care for her; she also bought cat food online and had it delivered home.
It's scary to think about the fact that less than six months ago, I was working my corporate job, clocking in with my badge, and now it's like: What comes next?Zoe De La Paz
De La Paz regularly contributes to her Robinhood and Acorns accounts and put $586 toward her savings and investments in July. She has an emergency savings fund of nearly $11,000, and a 401(k) from her previous employer that currently has more than $34,000 in it.
For now, De La Paz doesn't pay for health insurance, and says she has access to a low-cost employee clinic through work. One recent visit cost her just $15 to be seen for a head cold.
Life in Yellowstone: 'You're in nature's territory'
De La Paz has spent the majority of her life in the Midwest, growing up outside Peoria, Illinois, before attending the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and making her way to Chicago after graduation. Living in the mountains of the national park is unlike any other experience she's had.
"As much as I am a city girl and I love Chicago with my whole heart," she says, "I really feel like I'm connected and living with nature, and not [as] this separate being living outside of nature that then chooses when to dip her toes into it."
De La Paz recalls going on a hike on her second day in Yellowstone and coming across a grizzly bear. She often has to be on alert for potentially dangerous wildlife, including elk and bison, as she goes about her day.
"You're in nature's territory, not vice versa," she says, "and you have to have a lot of respect for that."
When she's not working, De La Paz enjoys free or low-cost activities put on by an employee resource group, like horseback riding, group hikes or a recent day trip to the Cody Rodeo that cost just $6 for the 3-hour bus ride and about $20 for entry.
Stitching together a new career
De La Paz's seasonal contract in Yellowstone runs until the end of September. As for what comes next, she says her sewing career is just taking off.
She's currently fielding a few job opportunities in Los Angeles that would involve working on film projects or concert touring productions, while in New York City she has leads on costuming gigs with regional theaters as well as a potential tailor job.
De La Paz says she plans to tap her $11,000 in savings to help with a move to one city or the other.
"It's scary to think about the fact that less than six months ago, I was working my corporate job, clocking in with my badge, and now it's like: What comes next?" she says.
De La Paz says her time in Yellowstone reconnected her with the possibility of making a career out of sewing.
"Being here has changed my life," she says.
De La Paz says moving to a new place where she knew no one reminded her that the world is big and there's a lot she's yet to experience; she's also a big believer in trusting that if she leaps, a net will appear.
"I know that regardless of where I end up, the work I will be doing will continue having me be behind a sewing machine," she says. "I'm excited for what comes next."

title: Cứu bệnh nhân bị hai thanh sắt đâm xuyên người
content:
Cứu bệnh nhân bị hai thanh sắt đâm xuyên người
Cần ThơNgười đàn ông chạy xe máy ngã vào công trường xây dựng bị hai thanh sắt đâm xuyên qua đùi và bụng, được bác sĩ bệnh viện ở Cần Thơ cứu sống.
Ngày 21/9, Bệnh viện Đa khoa Trung ương Cần Thơ cho biết bệnh nhân được đưa vào cấp cứu, chấn thương đe dọa tính mạng. Bệnh viện kích hoạt quy trình báo động đỏ nội viện, huy động êkíp liên chuyên khoa cứu bệnh nhân.
Trước đó, người dân tại hiện trường đã dùng máy cưa cắt ngắn hai thanh sắt rồi đưa nạn nhân đến Bệnh viện Đa khoa khu vực Ngã Bảy. Sau khi sơ cứu, bệnh nhân được chuyển lên Bệnh viện Đa khoa Trung ương Cần Thơ.
Êkíp Ngoại Tổng hợp do bác sĩ Huỳnh Dương Hữu Hạnh và bác sĩ Đỗ Minh Nhựt phẫu thuật cẩn trọng rút thanh sắt. Sau khi đánh giá tình trạng tổn thương phức tạp, các bác sĩ chuyển sang mổ mở cắt đoạn ruột non tổn thương, nối phục hồi lưu thông đường tiêu hóa.
Kế tiếp, êkíp Chấn thương chỉnh hình, do bác sĩ Nguyễn Hữu Thuyết - Trưởng khoa Phẫu thuật Cột sống và Chấn thương, cùng các cộng sự xử trí các tổn thương vùng đùi và rút thanh sắt cắm tại đây, cắt lọc phần cơ dập nát.
Sau khoảng 80 phút, ca phẫu thuật cấp cứu thành công. Bệnh nhân được chuyển về hồi sức ngoại tiếp tục theo dõi và điều trị, hiện tình trạng ổn. Tổng trọng lượng hai thanh sắt khi được lấy ra khoảng 2,5 kg.
Bác sĩ nhận định đây là tình huống đặc biệt, trong đó người bệnh đồng thời tổn thương tại ổ bụng, ruột non và nhiều cấu trúc phần mềm vùng đùi. Ca bệnh cũng cho thấy vai trò của xử lý ban đầu của tuyến trước, quy trình báo động đỏ nội viện và sự phối hợp đa chuyên khoa trong xử trí những trường hợp chấn thương xuyên thấu phức tạp.
Các bác sĩ khuyến cáo người dân khi xảy ra tai nạn có dị vật đâm xuyên cơ thể không tự ý rút dị vật ra, bởi thao tác này có thể làm tổn thương mạch máu, cơ quan nội tạng hoặc gây chảy máu ồ ạt. Khi đó, cần nhanh chóng đưa nạn nhân ra khỏi hiện trường an toàn, cố định dị vật, kịp thời chuyển đến tuyến cơ sở y tế có sự phối hợp đa chuyên khoa trong phẫu thuật, hồi sức chuyên sâu để được xử trí an toàn.

title: Citing barefoot Beed woman’s ‘struggle’, Bombay High Court gives mother children’s custody
content:
5 min readNew DelhiUpdated: Sep 7, 2026 03:30 PM IST

To afford her daughter’s education, 47-year-old Ramabai Ranvir ran three kilometres to win a Rs 3,000 cash prize in Maharashtra’s Beed district. Citing her extraordinary sacrifice while hearing a family matter, the Bombay High Court underlined the heavy burdens mothers often carry to secure their children’s future — and granted a woman custody of her two minor children.
Justice Rajesh S Patil said the incident was a “reminder” that a mother’s struggle to raise and educate her children is not always reflected merely in “figures” placed before the court. Behind those figures often lies a continuing “endeavour” to balance limited means against the ever-growing necessities of food, shelter, education and a dignified existence, he added.
“The court cannot remain ignorant of the realities of life which confront a woman who, while striving to secure the future of her children, is simultaneously required to attend to the necessities of her own day-to-day existence,” the September 3 order observed.
Noting that the husband himself, on a stamp paper, had admitted that he has an extramarital affair, the court held that in such circumstances, it could not be said that the children would be in a healthy environment in the father’s custody.
The high court was hearing a revision plea filed by the mother challenging a sessions court’s order that had granted interim custody of the two minor children to their father till the final disposal of the proceedings, while giving her only visitation rights.
Domestic violence complaint
The wife had filed a domestic violence complaint and an interim application seeking custody of her two children. The application was allowed after the judicial magistrate interviewed both children. Aggrieved, the husband challenged the order before the sessions court, which held that the allegation about the husband’s extramarital affair would not affect the interim application for custody of the minor children.
Justice Rajesh S Patil said the incident in Beed is a ‘reminder’ that a mother’s struggle to raise and educate her children is not always reflected merely in figures placed before the court.
The wife then filed this petition before the high court seeking interim custody of her daughter and son, claiming that she has recently joined the service of a company and earns a salary of Rs 13,000 per month.
Story continues below this ad
‘Children can live with grandparents’
The wife, through advocate Avesh Ghadge, claimed that her parents and her two married brothers live together, and both brothers have taken up the responsibility of her welfare, as well as that of her two children, both emotionally and financially.
She further claimed that her brothers’ children were around the same age as her own children and they would be able to enjoy each other’s company while living together with their maternal grandparents and uncles.
The woman alleged that both children were studying in a CBSE school. However, after the couple started living separately, the husband, whom she accused of often being drunk and also of having an extramarital affair, removed them from the school and admitted them to a state board school.
The husband, through his advocate Vijay V Patil, denied the allegations of an extramarital affair and that he was often inebriated. He submitted that both children were happily staying with him and their grandparents, who were taking care of them with love and affection. It was also argued that their present school was only around 100 to 150 metres from his residence.
Story continues below this ad
The man also claimed that his wife did not have an income source to meet the educational and other expenses of the children.
Children tutored, in-laws helpless: HC
The court found that the wife was not seeking custody as a means of obtaining financial support or any monetary advantage from her husband, as she had not claimed maintenance or alimony for herself. It noted that the daughter, being 12 years old and approaching puberty, would require more company of her mother, while the six-year-old son would also require his mother’s company.
After interacting with both children, the court found that they appeared to have been “tutored” by the husband. It also noted that the woman’s brothers had agreed and orally undertaken to take care of her and her children.
“They (wife and her brothers) do not require any kind of alimony or maintenance from respondent number 1 (husband) for their sister or towards her children,” the court noted.
Story continues below this ad
The court also interacted with the man’s parents and found them to be helpless. “As far as a healthy environment for the upbringing of the children is concerned, it is respondent number 1 (husband) who has, on a stamp paper, admitted that he has an extra-marital affair,” it added.
After considering the case, the court held that for the better future of the children and taking into account a better environment for them, the mother should get their custody.
The court directed the husband to hand over both children to the mother on September 9, and allowed the man to meet the children every Sunday till the final disposal of their case.

title: Дело «Хизмета»: Задержанный в Турции Эрмек Сабыржанов вернулся в Кыргызстан
content:
В Кыргызстан вернули Эрмека Сабыржанова — его 22 мая задержали в Турции. Он летел рейсом Бишкек-Анкара-Северный Кипр с женой и тремя детьми, когда турецкие правоохранители задержали его в аэропорту Эсенбога в Анкаре. Сабыржанова задержали по подозрению в связях с «Хизметом» — организацией давно умершего проповедника Фетхуллаха Гюлена. 9 сентября его наконец освободили и разрешили вернуться в Кыргызстан.
Аналогичный случай был в прошлом году, когда 20 апреля 2025 года кыргызстанец Азамат Нурмат уулу был задержан в Турции — тогда он, учитель математики, поехал со своими учениками на математическую олимпиаду в Анталье. Вернуться домой он смог только спустя 8 месяцев.
Нурмат уулу был учителем математики лицея имени Кусеина Карасаева на Иссык-Куле, филиала турецкого фонда «Маариф», подконтрольного властям Турции. Азамат Нурмат уулу восемь лет работал в «Сапате», с 2025 года поглощенного «Маарифом». До того он сам получал образование в связанном с сетью «Сапат» лицее в Кызыл-Кие, а также учился в Газиантепском университете в Турции.
«Сапат» до 2017 года был «Себатом». Это сеть учебных в заведений в разных странах мира, связанных с умершим в 2024 году проповедником Фетхуллахом Гюленом, бывшим соратником президента Турции Реджепа Эрдогана. После того, как их отношения испортились, Турция стала требовать закрытия этих учебных заведений в разных странах и преследовать ее сотрудников.
Так, например, в 2019 году Турция потребовала от властей Кыргызстана экстрадировать двух сотрудников «Сапата» Сенана Йылмаза и Санжара Абдулхакима. Но тогда Кыргызстан их не выдал.
С 2001 года гюленовские школы в Кыргызстане возглавлял Орхан Инанды. 31 мая 2021 года турецкие спецслужбы похитили его из Кыргызстана. Инанды пытали, обвинили в «руководстве вооруженной террористической организацией», и осудили на 21 год лишения свободы.

title: Conheça leis que garantem direitos às pessoas com deficiência no Distrito Federal
content:
O Dia Nacional de Luta da Pessoa com Deficiência é celebrado nesta segunda-feira (21). A data foi instituída pela Lei nº 11.133/2005 e reforça a garantia de direitos e a inclusão das pessoas com deficiência na sociedade.
No Distrito Federal, além da legislação nacional, existem normas específicas que estabelecem direitos em áreas como transporte, saúde, acessibilidade e circulação em espaços públicos e privados. Entre elas estão o Estatuto da Pessoa com Deficiência do DF, passe livre e leis que determinam adaptações.
As garantias previstas na legislação atravessam situações comuns do dia a dia, do deslocamento pela cidade ao atendimento em um hospital ou à realização de compras. Conhecer esses direitos ajuda a transformar normas que muitas vezes passam despercebidas em ferramentas de acesso, autonomia e participação social.
Lei Brasileira de Inclusão
Sancionada em 2015, a Lei nº 13.146/2015, conhecida como Lei Brasileira de Inclusão (LBI) ou Estatuto da Pessoa com Deficiência, estabelece normas para assegurar e promover, em condições de igualdade, o exercício dos direitos e das liberdades fundamentais das pessoas com deficiência.
A legislação aborda diferentes áreas da vida, como saúde, educação, trabalho, transporte, acessibilidade, cultura, lazer e participação social. Também estabelece medidas de combate à discriminação e determina atendimento prioritário em situações previstas pela lei.
A LBI define ainda a acessibilidade como condição para que a pessoa com deficiência possa utilizar, com segurança e autonomia, espaços, mobiliários, edificações, transportes, sistemas e meios de comunicação e informação.
Estatuto do DF reúne direitos e garante passe livre
No Distrito Federal, a Lei nº 6.637/2020 instituiu o Estatuto da Pessoa com Deficiência. A norma reúne direitos relacionados à saúde, educação, trabalho, assistência social, transporte, cultura, lazer, informação, comunicação e acessibilidade.
Entre as garantias está o transporte gratuito para pessoas com deficiência nas linhas de ônibus que integram as redes de transporte coletivo, mediante a comprovação do passe livre. A lei também determina que, nos casos de deficiência permanente, não seja necessário apresentar novamente o laudo médico na renovação do benefício, embora os demais documentos exigidos continuem sendo necessários.
O Estatuto também prevê o direito à saúde com atendimento personalizado e acessível, além da possibilidade de acompanhante durante períodos de atendimento e internação, salvo justificativa profissional de saúde em sentido contrário.
Hospitais devem ter macas e camas adaptadas
Uma situação menos conhecida está prevista na Lei nº 6.738/2020, que alterou a legislação distrital para garantir a disponibilização de macas e camas adaptadas para pacientes com deficiência e obesidade nas unidades hospitalares públicas e privadas do DF.
Os equipamentos devem estar disponíveis para internações e também para a realização de exames de saúde. A norma estabelece ainda que hospitais e unidades de pronto atendimento da rede pública, assim como estabelecimentos hospitalares privados, estejam preparados para receber pacientes com deficiência e adotem os meios de acessibilidade previstos na legislação.
Supermercados devem oferecer equipamentos adaptados
A acessibilidade também aparece na hora das compras. A Lei nº 6.420/2019 acrescentou à legislação distrital a obrigação de hipermercados, supermercados, centros comerciais e estabelecimentos semelhantes com área de vendas superior a 500 metros quadrados disponibilizarem equipamentos adaptados para pessoas com deficiência ou mobilidade reduzida.
A norma determina que 2% dos carrinhos de compras sejam adaptados para cadeirantes ou pessoas com mobilidade reduzida. Outros 2% devem ter assento de cadeirinha para crianças com deficiência ou mobilidade reduzida. Os estabelecimentos também devem disponibilizar pelo menos uma cadeira de rodas e indicar, por meio de placas, onde os equipamentos estão localizados.
Cão-guia tem acesso garantido a espaços de uso coletivo
A Lei nº 2.996/2002, posteriormente alterada pela Lei nº 5.876/2017, garante à pessoa com deficiência visual acompanhada de cão-guia o direito de entrar e permanecer com o animal em meios de transporte e em estabelecimentos abertos ao público, de uso público ou privado de uso coletivo.
A legislação considera ato de discriminação qualquer tentativa de impedir ou dificultar esse direito. A regra vale para estabelecimentos comerciais, industriais, de serviços e de saúde, além de outros espaços abrangidos pela norma.
Para utilizar o direito previsto na legislação distrital, a pessoa deve portar a identificação do cão-guia e a carteira de vacinação atualizada, além de utilizar o equipamento exigido para condução do animal.

title: [아시안게임] 테크볼 결승 진출한 이준석 "앞길 막막했는데…희망 발견"
content:
이준석, 테크볼 남자 단식 결승 진출
한국 테크볼 사상 첫 AG 메달 확보
"생업 포기 매진…선수 생활 희망 발견"
전체 내용을 이해하기 위해서는 기사 본문과 함께 읽어야 합니다.
송고 2026년09월19일 13시45분
이준석, 테크볼 남자 단식 결승 진출
한국 테크볼 사상 첫 AG 메달 확보
"생업 포기 매진…선수 생활 희망 발견"
구글 검색에서 연합뉴스 기사를 우선적으로 보여줍니다.
(나고야=연합뉴스) 김경윤 기자 = "가장 힘들었던 건 미래에 관한 걱정이었다."
한국 테크볼 사상 처음으로 아시안게임 메달을 확보한 이준석은 19일 일본 나고야 히가시 스포츠센터에서 열린 2026 아이치·나고야 아시안게임 테크볼 남자 단식 준결승에서 자이드 에이단(쿠웨이트)의 부상 기권으로 승리한 뒤 이렇게 말했다.
불모지나 다름없는 한국 테크볼에서 아시안게임 메달을 따겠다는 꿈을 위해 생업까지 포기했던 이준석은 "오늘 경기로 앞으로도 선수 생활을 이어갈 수 있다는 희망을 발견했다"며 "내일 열리는 결승에서 꼭 금메달을 따서 테크볼을 알리고, 우리 선수들이 걱정 없이 선수 생활을 이어갈 수 있는 발판을 만들고 싶다"고 밝혔다.
테크볼은 곡선형 특수 테이블에서 축구공을 주고받는 스포츠로, 2012년 헝가리에서 고안됐다.
주로 축구 선수들이 훈련 목적으로 즐기면서 관심을 끌었고, 2017년 국제테크볼연맹이 창설되면서 전문 스포츠 종목으로 자리 잡기 시작했다.
국내에선 2018년 대한테크볼협회가 설립됐으며, 주로 축구 혹은 족구 선수 출신이 생업과 병행하며 테크볼 선수로 활동하는 경우가 많다.
한국 테크볼의 에이스 이준석 역시 21살까지 K4리그에서 축구선수로 뛰다가 족구 선수를 거쳐 테크볼에 입문했다.
그는 대기업 생산직 계약직으로 일하다가 올해 2월 테크볼이 아시안게임 정식 종목으로 뒤늦게 채택됐다는 소식을 듣고 생업을 포기하고 훈련에 열중했다.
그는 "테크볼이 뒤늦게 정식 종목으로 포함되면서 다른 종목 선수들처럼 진천선수촌에 입촌하지 못하고 외부에서 대표팀 선수들과 함께 훈련했다"며 "열악한 환경에서도 쉬는 날 없이 매일 아침부터 저녁까지 훈련에 집중했는데 그 결실을 본 것 같아서 기쁘다"고 말했다.
이어 "훈련하면서 가장 힘들었던 건 메달을 못 따면 테크볼을 알리지 못하고 앞으로 살아갈 길도 막막해질 것이라는 공포였다"며 "최소한 결승에 진출하겠다는 생각으로 이번 대회에 임했고, 매일 밤 결승전을 치르는 모습을 꿈꿨다. 그 꿈을 이룬 것 같다"고 밝혔다.
이날 경기장엔 어머니 윤순정 씨와 누나가 찾아 이준석을 응원했다.
그는 "축구 선수 생활을 할 때는 가족들이 경기장에 오면 신경이 쓰여서 오지 말라고 했다"며 "하지만 이번 대회는 내 인생에서 다시 오기 어려운 무대인 것 같아서 가족들에게 와달라고 했다"고 소개했다.
그러면서 "경제적으로 힘들었던 20대 초반 테크볼 선수로 전향하면서 용기를 내 어머니에게 '나 테크볼 하고 싶어'라고 도움을 요청했고, 어머니는 없는 살림을 쪼개 200만원 상당의 테크볼 테이블을 구입해주셨다"며 "그때 기억이 많이 난다. 엄마에게 효도한 것 같아서 특히 기쁘다"고 말했다.
은메달을 확보한 이준석은 이제 20일 열리는 결승에서 금메달에 도전한다.
상대는 이라크의 강호 알리 잘릴 메즈헤르 알레야위다.
이준석은 "알레야위는 우승 후보로 꼽히는 선수이고 단식에선 한 번도 상대한 적이 없지만, 잘 알고 있는 선수"라며 "오늘 경기처럼 미친 듯이 몰입해 꼭 승리하겠다"고 다짐했다.
한편 이준석은 이날 경기 1세트를 12-10으로 마친 뒤 2세트 경기 중 상대 선수 에이단이 왼쪽 허벅지 근육 부상으로 기권하면서 승리했다.
경기 내내 득점 상황마다 큰 목소리를 내며 세리머니를 펼치던 이준석은 에이단이 일어나지 못하자 기쁜 내색 없이 경기장을 나왔다.
이후 휠체어를 타고 퇴장하는 에이단에게 다가가 허리를 굽히며 악수하고 위로했다.
이준석은 "그 선수도 큰 꿈을 안고 출전했을 것"이라며 "꿈에 그리던 결승에 진출하게 됐으나 그 상황에서는 안타까운 마음이 들더라"라고 말했다.

title: Children in 'birthplace' of Mary Poppins mark coming-of-age ritual
content:
'Birthplace' statue of Mary Poppins moves in Bowral's change-of-season ceremony
Each spring, children in the NSW Southern Highlands take part in an aging ritual that preserves their town's unique connection with one of the world's most beloved literary characters.
Australia-born author Helen Lyndon Goff, also known as PL Travers, spent her formative years in the town of Bowral.
Her experiences as a child, as well as the town's local characters, became the inspiration she would later draw on when creating the magical nanny Mary Poppins.
On Bowral Street, in Glebe Park, stands a 5-metre bronze statue of Mary Poppins, erected in 2012.
On the equinox, when the day is as long as the night, year 6 students turn the statue 180 degrees, the coming-of-age ritual reflecting their transition into high school.
Allana Winn, president of the Southern Highlands Youth Art Council, conducted the ceremony.
"Our year 6 students are here today and have been invited to the spring equinox turning to mark not just the changing of a season, but the new phase in their lives," she said.
Ms Winn reminded the children that everything changes with the wind, including visits from Mary Poppins, and that waiting periods and change are two of the hardest things for us to understand.
"Transitions are difficult, but change is exciting and inevitable. Embrace this rite of passage and be brave just like PL Travers and follow your dreams," she said.
'Birthplace' statue honours author
PL Travers was born in Maryborough, Queensland, but in 1907 moved with her family to Bowral, where she lived for 10 years.
Biographers say her time in the Southern Highlands was later the author's inspiration for Mary Poppins.
Paul McShane, with his daughter Melissa, initiated the concept of honouring the author's connection to the town with a Mary Poppins "birthplace statue" and he continues to be involved in the change-of-season ceremonies.
"In March we're talking about the coming winter, but in spring we're talking about the coming summer, which is when the Mary Poppins stories are set," he said.
"This park was opened in 1908, a year after they moved here, this was probably one of their very first experiences of a park, which is a central motif in the Mary Poppins stories."
An about-face for equinox
With eight books in the series, the nanny flies in on the east wind and out on the west wind, a feature the statue-turning ceremony replicates.
At the start of spring, year 6 children preparing for high school assist by turning the statue about face, using the built-in turntable.
"We invite children and leaders from the school to turn the statue around to celebrate, not just the coming summer but them going from primary school to high school," Mr McShane said.
"They all think it's pretty special."
Annalese Morris has five daughters and as one gets ready for university next year her middle child is preparing for high school, so changes are flying in all directions.
"I feel like when Mary Poppins says I'll go when the wind turns, it doesn't mean that life is predictable, it means you have to go with whatever comes," 12-year-old Maddie said.
"It's something special we get to do, it's a once-in-a-lifetime thing but there's always something new that will happen."
The Neleus Guild
Inspired by a moving statue included in the fourth book, Mary Poppins in the Park (1952), Mr McShane and friends spent five years causing a little mystery and hubbub of their own on the equinox.
"We don't know how exactly, but that statue got up and moved around the park," he said.
"We called ourselves the Neleus Guild, and we would come out here in the middle of the night and turn the statue.
"In fact, the deputy mayor, Gary Turland, phoned me one day and said, 'We're infuriated about this at upper council.
"'We're going to get to the bottom of this. We want these vandals caught'.
"And I had to explain, in a roundabout way, there was nothing to worry about," Mr McShane laughed.
By 2016, a turntable was erected in the park and the location of the statue changed again.
"She went on a jolly holiday and when she returned, there was this beautiful turntable built that she now sits on," Mr McShane said.
From one park to another
Loading...Australian sculptor Tanya Bartlett created the statue from a sketch proposed and modelled for by Travers herself.
"She wanted to see a statue of Mary Poppins in Central Park New York, but it never happened," Mr McShane said.
"In 1966, she talked to sculptor Sean Crampton in England, who sketched her holding the umbrella."
Mr McShane tracked down the sculptor's widow, who "remembered it all like it was yesterday".
"We got permission from her to use that design for our statue," he said.
"So, we built the statue that New York should have but never did."

title: Darmschrittmacher half - „Unkontrollierter Stuhlverlust belastete mich“
content:
Silvia Stechauner (69) litt jahrelang an unfreiwilligem Stuhlverlust. Dieses heikle Problem schränkte ihren Alltag stark ein und ließ sie aus Scham zur Einzelgängerin werden. Ein Darmschrittmacher gab ihr viele Freiheiten zurück. Nun möchte die Patientin anderen Betroffenen Mut machen. Wir haben sie und ihren Arzt Prim. Priv.-Doz. Dr. Stefan Riss getroffen.
„Vor allem beim Bücken und Heben konnte ich meinen Stuhl nicht mehr halten“, erzählt Silvia Stechauner offen über jene Symptome, die erstmals vor etwa 30 Jahren auftraten und die sie jahrelang aushielt. Jemand, der nicht an Stuhlinkontinenz leidet, kann sich mit Sicherheit nicht vorstellen, was das für Betroffene bedeutet. Frau Stechauner macht daher einen mutigen Schritt nach vorn und erzählt, wie sehr der unkontrollierte Stuhlverlust ihren Alltag beeinträchtigte – und ein Darmschrittmacher ihr Lebensfreude zurückgab.

title: Mahkamah Iran batal hukuman penjara penyanyi wanita
content:
Susulan kritikan hebat terhadap hukuman itu, mahkamah rayuan di ibu negara berkenaan membebaskan Hiwa Sefizadeh daripada tuduhan “menggalakkan rasuah dan pelacuran”, menurut laman sesawang berita Avash pada Rabu.
Sebaliknya, penyanyi itu dilaporkan dikenakan denda bersamaan lebih sedikit daripada USD200 serta tiga bulan khidmat masyarakat kerana “melanggar moral awam”.
Bulan lalu, Sefizadeh mendedahkan hukuman dijatuhkan terhadapnya berhubung konsert pada Februari 2025, susulan persembahannya bersama sebuah kumpulan muzik yang memainkan muzik klasik Parsi sebelum acara itu dihentikan pasukan keselamatan.
Persembahan awam oleh penyanyi wanita secara umumnya tidak dibenarkan di Iran.
Penyanyi itu berkongsi satu hantaran di Instagram daripada peguamnya yang mengesahkan pengurangan hukumannya.
“Semoga tiba hari apabila tiada lagi suara dibisukan,” katanya dalam hantaran itu.
Hukuman penjara itu mendapat kritikan meluas, dengan Sefizadeh turut mendapat sokongan daripada sektor kebudayaan.
“Kita mempunyai begitu ramai penyanyi wanita berbakat dan begitu banyak karya bernilai dihasilkan,” kata Hamid Reza Noorbakhsh, pengarah Persatuan Artis House of Music, ketika itu.
Menurutnya, tiada peraturan agama dan undang-undang di Iran yang secara asasnya dan tanpa pengecualian melarang wanita menyanyi.

title: 21 police, ICA, auxiliary officers lauded for rejecting bribes, reporting corruption
content:
21 police, ICA, auxiliary officers lauded for rejecting bribes, reporting corruption
- 21 officers from the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority, police, Certis, and AETOS were honoured for rejecting bribes and reporting corruption.
- The Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau reported 68 corruption cases in 2025, with 22 involving public officers rejecting bribes.
- Senior Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office Desmond Tan urged companies to assess risks and uphold good governance to protect Singapore's reputation.
AI generated
SINGAPORE – When Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officer Ernest Low was offered a bribe at Changi Airport, he knew it would be a long day as he would have to question the traveller.
The man, a Chinese national who had earlier been stopped by ICA from entering Singapore, handed Low a $100 bill on the afternoon of March 2, 2025, in an attempt to remain here.
On Sept 18, 2026, at the Raffles City Convention Centre, Low was one of 21 officers from ICA, the Singapore Police Force, Certis and Aetos who were lauded for preventing and reporting corrupt practices.
In the 2025 incident, after Low was offered the money, he asked the traveller what it was for. The man said he had spent money to travel to Singapore from Kuala Lumpur and did not want his prior bookings to be in vain.
Low rejected the bribe, informed him that this was a crime and detained him. The 36-year-old traveller was sentenced to three weeks’ jail in April 2025.
Senior Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office Desmond Tan presented the awards at the 2026 event organised by the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB).
He commended the officers for having integrity at work, even when people do not notice.
Low, 29, who is now a manager in the policy and development division at ICA, said of the 2025 case: “My immediate reaction was to make sure that I rejected his bribe very clearly so it would be clear to everybody that ICA officers act with integrity.”
Releasing its annual statistics on April 28, the CPIB said 68 cases were registered for investigation in 2025, down from 75 in 2024 and 81 the previous year. Of the 68 cases registered for investigation in 2025, 22 involved public service officers rejecting bribes.
The theme of the Sept 18 event was “Advancing Anti-Corruption for Trust and Business Growth”.
Tan said: “We still hear, from time to time, that anti-corruption measures burden businesses by slowing processes and adding costs. I do understand and appreciate these sentiments, but those who think this way may have the equation backwards. Companies with good governance are better able to manage risks and attract trusted partners.”
He added that over the past decade, construction, manufacturing, transport and storage were among the main industries vulnerable to private sector corruption.
According to CPIB, a gift given innocently and without any corrupt intention is not considered corruption.
But if a gift is given or received with a view to securing or reciprocating, for example, an unfair advantage, it may be considered an act of corruption.
Tan noted that many companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, want to do the right thing but are unsure of where to start.
To this, he said CPIB has resources to help companies assess risks and review policies, while trade associations and industry leaders can help businesses understand risks and share their experiences with peers.
He also urged organisations to assess corruption risks, close gaps and strengthen standards, with compliance teams, business leaders and industry bodies each playing a role in driving improvements.
He said: “We built Singapore’s clean reputation together through choices to do the right thing, even when it’s inconvenient. It belongs to all of us, and we must protect it together.”
You can report corruption to CPIB on its website or by calling its hotline on 1800-376-0000.
You can also e-mail report@cpib.gov.sg or visit or write to CPIB Headquarters at 2 Lengkok Bahru, Singapore 159047.

title: L’expulsion « en urgence absolue » de l’influenceur algérien « Doualemn » annulée par le tribunal administratif de Paris
content:
L’expulsion « en urgence absolue » de l’influenceur algérien « Doualemn », condamné pour « incitation à la violence », a été annulée par le tribunal administratif de Paris, qui a également annulé le retrait de son titre de séjour, selon une décision consultée vendredi 18 septembre par l’Agence France-Presse (AFP).
Boualem Naman, connu sous le pseudonyme de Doualemn, avait été arrêté à Montpellier en mars 2025 pour avoir appelé à « donner une sévère correction » à un opposant au régime algérien dans une vidéo postée sur le réseau social TikTok le 4 janvier 2025. En juillet dernier, la cour d’appel de Montpellier a confirmé le jugement en première instance en condamnant l’influenceur de 61 ans, qui ne cache pas ses sympathies pour le gouvernement d’Alger, à cinq mois de prison avec sursis pour « incitation à la violence ». Il faisait toujours l’objet d’un arrêté d’expulsion pris en janvier 2025 par le ministre de l’intérieur de l’époque, Bruno Retailleau.
Lors de l’audience, le 3 septembre 2026, au sujet de cet arrêté, l’avocate de Doualemn, Me Vanessa Edberg, avait déploré que son client ait été « utilisé comme un pion politique ». « M. Retailleau s’est précipité sans examen sérieux du dossier et s’est servi du pouvoir judiciaire à des fins politiques », avait-elle dénoncé. L’interpellation de l’influenceur avait été annoncée sur le réseau social X par l’ex-ministre de l’intérieur et actuel président du parti Les Républicains, Bruno Retailleau, partisan d’une ligne dure face à Alger, qu’Emmanuel Macron a récemment dénoncée.
Dans son jugement, le tribunal administratif a estimé vendredi que les éléments rapportés par le ministère de l’intérieur « ne pouvaient suffire à démontrer que la présence de Boualem Naman, qui représente certes une menace grave pour l’ordre public (…), ferait peser un risque immédiat au point de justifier son expulsion en urgence absolue, alors qu’en outre l’autorité judiciaire n’a pas estimé utile de le placer en détention provisoire ni même sous contrôle judiciaire dans l’attente de son procès ». « Dans ces conditions, (…) le ministre de l’intérieur a entaché sa décision d’irrégularité », poursuit le tribunal.
Le tribunal conclut que « la décision d’expulsion de M. Naman (…) doit être annulée ainsi que, par voie de conséquence, les décisions du même jour lui retirant son titre de séjour et fixant l’Algérie comme pays d’éloignement ».
Le tribunal ne s’est en revanche pas prononcé sur la demande d’annulation d’un second arrêté d’expulsion, mais qui n’invoquait pas l’urgence absolue. M. Naman peut donc toujours être potentiellement renvoyé de France. Son avocate Me Vanessa Edberg étudie la possibilité de saisir la cour administrative d’appel, a-t-elle indiqué vendredi à l’AFP.

title: New centre offers hope in community with high DV rates
content:
New men's centre in Kalumburu aimed at reducing domestic violence
In short:
Western Australia's northernmost community has opened a centre for men in a bid to curb its domestic violence rate.
Kalumburu police and residents collaborated to create The Men's Place.
What's next?
The centre still needs furniture in order to accommodate overnight stays.
A new men's space has been created in a remote West Australian community in a bid to curb its domestic violence rate, which is one of the highest in the country.
With the Benyjin Gulaali (The Men's Place) opening in Kalumburu, more than 3,000 kilometres north of Perth, there is hope it will increase safety in the community.
Police data shows that in 2026 there have been 46 domestic and family violence incidents in Kalumburu.
The total of 193 offences against a person in 2025 was the highest number for the 400-person community in the past 10 years.
Sergeant Brian Welch, one of two police officers in Kalumburu, has seen a shortage of services for people involved in domestic violence incidents.
"There's nothing for men here at all in the community," he said.
He said police often offered support to struggling men, which could be "a cup of tea and a chat" at the police station, to de-escalate tension that could otherwise lead to violence.
"We try to talk to them before you get to that space where there's violence involved," Sergeant Welch said.
But Sergeant Welch has long been advocating for men to have a dedicated space and support.
A place to open up
The men's space will offer emergency accommodation, support and community, and, for now, is open three mornings a week.
"It's my idea, but it's a community thing," Sergeant Welch said.
The project started from talks with community members such as Jeremy Kowan.
"We've been waiting for that for a few years, now it's up and going," he said.
Mr Kowan said men who were struggling with relationships and a lack of support services used to turn to him and other elders for advice.
"I used to talk my way through to them, tell them 'just don't worry'," he said.
"Just think about you, your family, your young ones. Think about them, their future ahead and just don't worry about the outside things."
Mr Kowan is excited Kalumburu men now have a dedicated space.
"The women got their own place, the men got their own place now," he said.
"The men are all starting to like that place, and every time I drive past I see them relaxing on the lounges, and talking away and laughing … it's really good."
Small community, big problem
Kalumburu has fewer than 400 residents, making the need for a space for men more pronounced.
Sergeant Welch said enforcing restriction orders, which aimed to guarantee safety for victims, was a challenge.
"If they get served with police orders, they have to leave their home and there's really nowhere for them to go other than to other family members," he said.
In Kalumburu, houses are often overcrowded, with multiple generations and extended families forced to live under one roof.
Colleen Zulian, who runs Kalumburu Strong Women Centre, said sometimes offenders had nowhere to go and ended up on the streets or back with their partners.
"Most houses are overcrowded, so that in itself gives restrictions to them going to another house," she said.
"When there's an FDV situation, the mother and all the kids have to come."
Lack of support 'contributes to DV'
Ms Zulian has been supporting women in the community for years.
"The men haven't had any support, which contributes to DV and family disagreements," she said.
Ms Zulian said more counselling could help healing and turning things around for this generation and the next.
"Hopefully more services will come because now they have a space where they can reach the men," she said.
The centre has not reached its full potential and still needs furniture to offer emergency accommodation, but it has already provided employment and hope for a brighter future.
"We can do that, help the families, stop people from violence," Mr Kowan said.
"Because that's not good for the young ones, whilst they are growing up they are looking at violence.
"We need to stop them from doing that, sit down and have a talk with them."

title: Woman gives birth beside dinosaur display outside Pattaya mall
content:
Woman gives birth beside dinosaur display outside Pattaya mall
A woman gave birth unexpectedly outside a Pattaya shopping centre, where a newborn girl was found beside a dinosaur display before rescuers located the exhausted mother inside the mall.
The Sawang Boriboon rescue foundation was alerted on September 19 to the newborn outside Central Beach Festival on Pattaya Second Road.
Rescuers found the baby lying near fencing around a dinosaur display with the umbilical cord still attached. She was initially silent but began crying after responders moved in to help.
Motorcycle taxi drivers nearby brought cloth to cover the baby and held her while emergency services were contacted.
The mother, a 40 year old woman from Bangkok, was initially nowhere to be found.
Mall security and rescue workers searched the area before locating her exhausted in a ground-floor toilet. Rescuers said the placenta had been discarded in a bin.
The woman and her baby were then taken to Pattaya Hospital.
Initial examinations found both were safe but required close observation. The mother was suffering from heavy bleeding and severe exhaustion, reported Siam Chon News.
She told officials this was her third pregnancy and estimated she had been around seven to eight months pregnant.
The woman said she developed severe abdominal pain while sitting outside the mall that morning before suddenly giving birth. She then went into the shopping centre to wash herself before rescuers found her.
Motorcycle taxi driver Suchat said the woman staggered towards the dinosaur display and appeared to be pushing before suddenly giving birth. Bystanders rushed to help the newborn and call emergency services, while the mother walked away and was later found inside the mall.

title: Jazz-Nachwuchs: Leander sorgt für den Groove [premium]
content:
Er ist einer der jüngsten Musiker der Klosterneuburger Big Band: Leander Raab (17) spielt sehr erfolgreich mehrere Instrumente und erzählt, wieso sich das Üben auszahlt.
Wenn sich bei der Ballnacht zum 60-Jahr-Jubiläum der Musikschule alle auf der Tanzfläche drängeln, steht er auf der Bühne: Leander Raab (17) ist mit seinem Saxofon einer der jüngsten Musiker der Jazz-Big-Band. Und wahrscheinlich einer der vielseitigsten: Neben Saxofon spielt er auch E-Bass, Tuba und Klavier. Wie kam es dazu? „Ich habe vor zehn Jahren an der Musikschule mit Saxofon begonnen. Dann kamen die anderen Instrumente dazu. Mir machen alle Spaß, ich könnte mich nicht für eines entscheiden,“ sagt der junge Mann. Leander ist schon auf vielen Bühnen gestanden: mit dem Ensemble „Jumping jungle“ im Wiener Jazzclub Porgy und Bess, mit dem Jugend Jazz-Orchester NÖ in Grafenegg, mit den Funky Spaghetti oder den „Young Masters“ der MdW (Universität für Musik und darstellende Kunst Wien).
Mit anderen gemeinsam zu proben und auf der Bühne zu stehen – das sind für Leander die schönsten Aspekte des Musizierens. „Man lernt Freunde kennen durch eine gemeinsame Aktivität. Man muss nicht einmal die gleiche Sprache sprechen.“ Wie ist es mit dem Üben? Wie motiviert er sich dazu? „Ich musste mich nie großartig motivieren. Beim Jazz lohnt es sich einfach, dranzubleiben. Wenn man sich hinsetzt und ein paar Stunden was macht, erreicht man einen Level, wo man sich kreativ ausbreiten kann.“ Anders als die klassische Musik, lebt der Jazz vom Improvisieren: Die Musiker haben zwar Jazz-Standards bekannter Jazz-Größen als Ausgangsmaterial, dann kommt es aber darauf an, die Melodien zu umspielen und zu variieren, dabei die Rhythmen zu verändern und sich andere Phrasierungen einfallen zu lassen. Daher weiß man zu Beginn eines Konzerts nie, wie es am Ende klingt und kein Abend gleicht dem anderen.
Die Liebe zur Musik war Leander quasi in die Wiege gelegt. Sein Vater ist Solotrompeter an der Wiener Volksoper und in der Jazz-Szene fest verankert, seine Mutter unterrichtet Klavier und auch seine beiden Schwestern sind musikalisch. An der Musikschule Klosterneuburg traf er auf engagierte und motivierte Lehrerinnen und Lehrer. Die Erfolge ließen nicht auf sich warten: Beim Musikwettbewerb Prima la Musica erreichte Leander viermal den ersten Platz. Will er die Musik zu seinem Beruf machen? „Ich will die Musik schon irgendwie einbringen.“ Derzeit besucht er noch die „Graphische“, eine Schule für Berufe der visuellen Kommunikation und Medientechnik. „Auch Film und Technik interessieren mich sehr.“ Wer Leander live auf der Bühne erleben will, hat am 3. Oktober in der Babenbergerhalle die Gelegenheit: Er spielt im Orchester und in der Big Band.
»Beim Jazz lohnt es sich, dranzubleiben. Wenn man sich ein paar Stunden hinsetzt und was macht, erreicht man einen Level, wo man sich kreativ ausbreiten kann.«
Tipp.
Jubiläums-Ball. Beim Ball zum 60-Jahr Jubiläum der Musikschule Klosterneuburg spielt Leander Raab in der Big Band. Außerdem gibt es ein großes Salonorchester, Heurigenmusik, einen DJ und vieles mehr. 3. Oktober, Babenbergerhalle Klosterneuburg, Tickets zu 35 Euro unter musikschule-klosterneuburg/musikschulball

title: Cuban Woman with I-220A Shares Experience After ICE Appointment: "Many Were Wearing Ankle Monitors"
content:
A Cuban woman residing in the United States recently took to Instagram to share her experience before and after her annual appointment with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), sparking a wave of support among thousands of fellow Cubans who share similar uncertainties.
Leyla González, who entered the U.S. through the border in 2021 and holds an I-220A document, posted a video the night before her appointment. Speaking calmly and honestly, she confessed to feeling something that hadn't happened in years of uneventful appointments: "Nothing has ever happened to me before. But this year, I must admit I'm extremely nervous."
The influencer decided to record her thoughts because she knew she wasn't alone: "I know many of you might feel the same way and can relate to my situation because you're going through exactly what I am."
Leyla's experience is just one of many faced by Cubans with I-220A in the U.S. Stay updated on ICE appointments, immigration forms, and news in U.S. immigration.
Her initial video garnered over 326,000 views, highlighting the significant impact of this issue within the Cuban exile community.
After her appointment, Leyla shared a second video expressing gratitude for the overwhelming support on social media, and detailed what transpired inside the ICE office.
Arriving at 7:45 am for her 8:00 am appointment, she encountered a long line outside. Inside, she noticed a distinct separation: "They divided the Cubans on one side into a line and the other nationalities into another. Then they called the other nationalities first, leaving the Cubans waiting."
Eventually, all Cubans present had their documents collected and were moved to a different waiting area, where they remained for hours without information. An officer then began calling each person individually to return their documents with the outcome.
For Leyla, the result was the best she could hope for: "They gave me my document and scheduled me for the same date next year. I didn't see any detentions, and no one was taken into custody," she shared.
However, she did observe something that underscores the current migration tension: "There were many Cubans wearing ankle monitors, as well as people from other nationalities like Venezuelans and Nicaraguans; many were wearing ankle monitors."
She concluded with a heartfelt message to those still awaiting their turn: "If you're waiting for your ICE appointment, I wish you the best of luck and send a big kiss, because I know how it feels."
This testimony comes at a time of significant uncertainty for I-220A holders. In 2026, ICE appointments have had varied outcomes: some Cubans leave without issues, while others face deportation orders or expedited removal after attendance.
The I-220A is a supervised release order allowing individuals to remain out of custody while their immigration case is pending. However, it is not equivalent to parole and does not grant a definitive immigration status, leaving hundreds of thousands of Cubans in legal limbo.
Last week, it was revealed that a lawsuit in Miami could pave the way to residency for I-220A holders: Federal Judge Jacqueline Becerra rejected the government's attempt to dismiss the Bello-Rubio vs. DHS lawsuit, filed by 992 Cubans, which seeks to have the I-220A recognized as parole to qualify for residency under the Cuban Adjustment Act. If successful, the case could benefit between 500,000 and 600,000 Cubans.
Understanding the I-220A and Its Implications
What is the I-220A document?
The I-220A is a supervised release order that allows individuals to remain out of custody while their immigration case is being processed. It does not provide a permanent legal status.
Why are Cuban nationals concerned about their ICE appointments?
Cuban nationals are concerned because ICE appointments have produced mixed results, with some individuals facing deportation orders or expedited removal, leading to significant uncertainty about their future in the U.S.
How could the Miami lawsuit impact I-220A holders?
The lawsuit in Miami seeks to have the I-220A recognized as parole, which would allow holders to apply for residency under the Cuban Adjustment Act. If successful, it could benefit hundreds of thousands of Cubans.

title: Entre a ambição de chegar às estrelas e a vontade de explorar novos horizontes: Que futuro imaginam os jovens astronautas por um dia?
content:
Este domingo, 35 jovens tiveram a oportunidade de flutuar em gravidade zero, num voo parabólico que, durante alguns minutos, permitiu recriar a sensação de estar no Espaço. Para alguns dos estudantes que participaram na mais recente edição da iniciativa organizada pela Agência Espacial Portuguesa, a experiência confirmou uma ambição que têm desde crianças e, para outros, abriu possibilidades que ainda não tinham considerado para o seu futuro.
Não perca nenhuma notícia importante da atualidade de tecnologia e acompanhe tudo em tek.sapo.pt
“É uma sensação fenomenal”, conta Rodrigo Rodrigues, ao TEK Notícias, embora admita que esta é uma experiência difícil de traduzir totalmente em palavras. “A liberdade que temos de andar no teto e de caminhar nas paredes, é como se estivéssemos a voar. É uma coisa que não dá para explicar”, realça
Entre os jovens com quem falámos, há também quem descreva a experiência de estar em gravidade zero como algo “surreal”, como se o “corpo saísse de si próprio e andasse à deriva”. “É não sentir absolutamente nada à nossa volta: fechamos os olhos e não sentimos nada”, conta Isabel Gomes.
Para os estudantes, a experiência afirmou-se como o culminar de um processo que começou muito antes de vestirem os fatos de astronauta e de entrarem no avião. Os jovens que participaram passaram por um processo de seleção extenso, que incluiu testes de memória, velocidade e raciocínio espacial, bem como provas físicas e uma entrevista final.
“É muito gratificante”, conta Leonor Costa. “Foi a recompensa do nosso esforço durante quatro meses”, acrescenta Rodrigo Rodrigues.
Antes do voo, que decorreu pela segunda vez em Santa Maria, nos Açores, os jovens passaram alguns dias em atividades de grupo para incentivar o trabalho em equipa e reforçar laços, incluindo formações acerca do sector espacial.
Clique nas imagens para ver com mais detalhe
Na véspera, houve tempo para conhecerem os grupos onde ficariam, para experimentar os fatos pela primeira vez e para visitar o interior do avião, um Airbus A310 operado pela francesa Novespace, em preparação para o voo parabólico.
Recorde-se que, num voo como este, o avião sobe até cerca de seis mil metros de altitude antes de iniciar uma série de manobras de ascensão e queda, ou parábolas.
Ao longo destas manobras, são recriados diferentes ambientes de gravidade, com várias atividades pelo meio, como experiências com água e acrobacias no ar. Na primeira fase, os passageiros sentem os efeitos da gravidade como se estivessem em Marte e, na segunda, na Lua.
Na terceira fase é possível experimentar uma sensação de gravidade zero, em ciclos de cerca de 20 segundos. Nos voos, com uma duração típica a rondar duas horas, são realizadas 15 parábolas, com os jovens a experimentarem entre cinco a seis minutos de gravidade zero.
Confirmar sonhos e abrir novos horizontes espaciais
Para alguns dos participantes, a experiência serviu para confirmar a ambição de ter uma carreira no sector do Espaço. “Desde pequeno que sempre disse que queria ser astronauta”, conta Tomás Benta. “Acho que esta experiência só vem confirmar a minha expectativa de que é mesmo isto que eu quero seguir no futuro”, afirma, numa visão partilhada por Cármen Marto, que também sonha em ser astronauta.
Já Maria Takimura descreve a experiência como “uma motivação e um abrir de olhos” para a área espacial, que a deixou “muito mais interessada, com vontade de saber mais e de experienciar mais”.
Muitos dos jovens com quem falámos seguem já percursos ligados às áreas STEM e viram na sua participação uma oportunidade para confirmar interesses que tinham antes da experiência.
Mas a ligação ao sector espacial não depende necessariamente de uma carreira científica ou na engenharia e há jovens interessados em gestão, matemática ou outras áreas que também imaginam um futuro ligado à indústria espacial.
Isabel Gomes, por exemplo, já sabe que, quando chegar à universidade quer entrar na área da Matemática. “Se pudesse conciliar as duas coisas, a minha paixão pelo espaço e a minha grande paixão pela Matemática, seria um sonho”, explica.
Já para Rodrigo, que, desde criança que tinha uma ideia bastante definida de seguir o caminho da Medicina, a experiência abriu novos horizontes. Embora não tenha mudado de planos, a iniciativa fê-lo pensar em possibilidades que até então não tinha considerado.
Os estudantes que participaram nesta edição do Astronauta por um Dia juntam-se agora ao grupo de embaixadores da iniciativa que, segundo dados partilhados pela Agência Espacial Portuguesa, conta já com 146 jovens.
Recorde-se que a quinta edição da iniciativa foi também a mais concorrida até à data. Depois de mais de 500 candidaturas no ano passado, a iniciativa recebeu este ano 762 inscrições, superando também o anterior recorde de 634 candidaturas, registado em 2023. Entre os candidatos estavam 380 raparigas e 382 rapazes, na maioria com idades entre os 15 e os 16 anos.
Dos 762 candidatos, apenas 25 portugueses chegaram à fase final. A eles juntaram-se também, pela primeira vez, estudantes de outro país europeu, com 10 jovens vindos da Estónia.
Segundo a Agência Espacial Portuguesa, a iniciativa do Astronauta por um Dia foi já foi replicada em países como Luxemburgo, Áustria, Estónia, França e Espanha, e, em breve, poderá realizada também na Grécia e República Checa.

title: Journée sans voiture à Bruxelles : “Les automobilistes ont changé de comportement” (PHOTOS)
content:
Journée sans voiture à Bruxelles : "Les automobilistes ont changé de comportement" (PHOTOS)
Des affaires à transporter ou une crainte pour la sécurité : des blocages persistent pour se mettre au vélo, mais les infrastructures se sont visiblement améliorées.
- Publié le 20-09-2026 à 15h24
- Mis à jour le 20-09-2026 à 16h01
La journée a commencé sous une pluie battante mais dès les premiers rayons de soleil, vers midi, les cyclistes, joggeurs et promeneurs se sont emparés des routes bruxelloises libérées des voitures le temps d'une journée.
"Une excellente initiative" pour Joshua, étudiant de 25 ans qui se réjouit de l'introduction d'une deuxième journée sans voiture dès 2027. "C'est un moment pour se réapproprier des espaces qui sont réservés aux voitures tout le reste de l'année."
Journée sans voiture à Bruxelles : “Les automobilistes ont changé de comportement”
"Plus rapide que la voiture," il utilise le vélo pour tous ses trajets quotidiens depuis cinq ans. "C'est moins cher et plus efficace." Au fil des années il a noté de belles améliorations des infrastructures pour les cyclistes. "Il y a de plus en plus de pistes séparées de la circulation automobile. Mais cela reste encore bien différent de certaines villes notamment en Flandre. Il y a encore beaucoup de moments où les pistes cyclables s'arrêtent et obligent les cyclistes à revenir sur la route. Ce sont souvent les situations les plus dangereuses. Mais le vélo est accessible tout de même à Bruxelles."
Autour du rond-point Montgomery nous rencontrons aussi Beatrijs et Jean-Safran. Elle, ne roule quasiment jamais à vélo. "J'ai souvent beaucoup de choses à transporter donc je suis surtout en voiture." Lui, pédale tous les deux à trois jours, "pour le plaisir" : "De mes 14 à mes 21 ans je faisais tous mes trajets à vélo. Je remarque quand même que les automobilistes ont changé de comportement. Plus jeune, j'ai failli me faire choper plusieurs fois par des voitures qui ne vérifiaient pas leur angle mort. Aujourd'hui ça ne m'arrive plus."
"On a déjà eu des choses mal pensées"
Les deux trentenaires notent des améliorations pour les cyclistes "comme ici à Montgomery mais il reste encore des points noirs, comme Meiser."
Le jeune cycliste occasionnel note tout de même que les aménagements cyclables ne doivent pas faire oublier la voiture : "Il y a des professions qui ont absolument besoin d'un véhicule, des petits indépendants, il ne faut pas les oublier. Mais je suppose qu'ils ont fait une étude de mobilité pour le projet de réaménagement de Meiser. Parce qu'on a déjà eu des choses mal pensées comme le piétonnier. Ne pas prévoir de piste cyclable pour cet axe qui traverse tout Bruxelles, ça crée des situations aujourd'hui où les piétons doivent faire attention à chaque fois aux vélos sur le piétonnier."
"Dans notre appartement ce n'est pas facile de stocker les vélos"
Pour beaucoup, la journée sans voiture est aussi l'occasion de s'essayer à la bicyclette. C'est le cas de Dominique et Adèle, sa fille de 11 ans qui va bientôt partir en classe verte et s'exerce donc. "On ne roule jamais à vélo. Je trouve que ce n'est pas très sécurisé," nous dit notamment la mère de famille. "Mais ici c'est l'occasion. On a surtout un problème de place. Dans notre appartement ce n'est pas facile de stocker les vélos." Pour la famille la journée est idéale.
"On fait tout avec la STIB," poursuit Dominique. "On est bien lotis à Bruxelles en termes de transports en commun. On n'a pas de voiture. Parfois ça peut être utile pour un déménagement ou pour des courses mais au quotidien ça ne manque pas."
En tout cas, le "test vélo" en aura convaincu une ce dimanche : "C'est vraiment chouette. Je préfère largement le vélo à la marche," conclut Adèle.

title: Venezuela supera el centenar de medallas en los Juegos Suramericanos Santa Fe 2026
content:

Dos oros y un bronce fue el balance, con el ciclismo y el atletismo como protagonistas.

Por su parte, Ottanys Febres, con un tiro de 51.98 metros fue tercera en el lanzamiento de disco, disciplina en la que el triunfo fue para la brasileña Andressa Oliveira, cuyo mejor registro fue 59.36 metros. La plata fue para la colombiana Yerlin Mesa (55.49m).
Así, Venezuela llegó este martes a 102 preseas en los Juegos Suramericanos Santa Fe 2026, 33 de ellas de oro, 34 de plata y 35 de bronce para afianzarse en el cuarto puesto de la general.
Brasil comanda el medallero con 201 metales, 82 de oro; seguido por Argentina (184-48) y Colombia (124-44).

title: ‘Preventive detention can’t replace criminal law’: High Court quashes PSA against Srinagar man
content:
4 min readSep 21, 2026 03:37 PM IST

Preventive detention cannot become a substitute for ordinary criminal law, the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court has said as it quashed the Public Safety Act (PSA) invoked against a Srinagar resident.
“Preventive detention cannot become a substitute for ordinary criminal law. Nor can the extraordinary power of preventive detention be exercised merely because the authorities entertain a general apprehension regarding a person’s antecedents,” Justice M A Chowdhary said in his judgment on September 17. “There must be material from which a rational prognosis of future prejudicial conduct can be made”.
Zubair Altaf Sheikh, a resident of Soura, Srinagar, was booked under the controversial Public Safety Act (PSA) in September last year, primarily on the back of an FIR registered against him in 2022. While he had been bailed out by the court in the case, the same case was used to book him under the Public Safety Act (PSA) for the first time in 2022. The detention, too, had been quashed by the court.




While counsel for the respondents argued that the PSA detention order is not “founded merely upon the FIR” registered in 2022 and has been based on a fresh dossier containing more materials and “fresh inputs received through discrete sources”, Justice Chowdhary said the “court is unable to accept the submission”.
“An antecedent can undoubtedly be referred to for a limited purpose, but where the antecedent is relied upon as a circumstance supporting the conclusion that the detenue continues to pose a threat to the ‘security of the State’, it must have a live and proximate nexus with the present necessity of detention,” the court said.
Those discreet police records, it said, correspond to the time period when the petitioner was working in Delhi as a store manager with Blinkit.
“Another significant circumstance is that the detenue was working as a Store Manager at Gurugram, Delhi. The assertion that he was in Delhi in connection with his employment has remained un-rebutted. Petitioner has placed on record documents in support of his assertion of being in Gurugram NCR Delhi, having received wages for the period regarding which discreet reports were made foundational basis to pass impugned detention order,” the court said.
Story continues below this ad
While employment at another place cannot, by itself, negate allegations of prejudicial activity, “it was nevertheless a relevant circumstance which required due consideration by the detaining authority, while assessing whether there existed a continuing and immediate threat warranting preventive detention,” the court said.
Referring to Sheikh’s earlier PSA order being quashed in April 2024, the court said the “judicial development was a material circumstance which necessarily required consideration while assessing the present detention”.
“The detaining authority could not mechanically revive the earlier narrative without demonstrating how the subsequent material overcame the effect of the passage of time and established a fresh and continuing threat,” the judgment read.
Referring to the various Supreme Court judgments, Justice Chowdhary said that the “underlying principle in cases of preventive detention is the existence of a live and proximate link” between the grounds of detention and the confirmed purpose of detention and an unexplained delay can snap such link and render the subjective satisfaction vulnerable.
Story continues below this ad
“A mere description of a person by a particular label, without particulars of the acts which constitute the alleged prejudicial conduct, cannot by itself furnish an adequate basis for preventive detention. The constitutional requirement is that the grounds must be sufficiently specific to enable the detenue to understand and effectively meet the allegations,” it said. “In the present case, the FIR of 2022, viewed against the subsequent quashing of the earlier PSA detention order, the passage of nearly three years, the unrebutted assertion regarding the detenue’s employment at Gurugram, and the absence of specific contemporaneous acts attributable to him, cannot by itself furnish the requisite live link”.

title: Derby men’s soccer team secures first win
content:
Derby’s men’s senior soccer team has cause for celebration after recording its first-ever win as a club with a 4-1 victory over Fitzroy Crossing Social Soccer on Sunday.
The match was the fourth game of the year for the Derby side and only the second time the two teams had met, making the result an important moment for soccer in the local community.
The convincing victory marks a significant step forward for Derby soccer, with the senior men’s team continuing to build momentum and interest in the sport.
The club also thanked Derby District High School for allowing the team to use its facilities for the meeting and for its ongoing support of soccer in the community.
There could be more exciting times ahead, with Derby Town Oval recently receiving upgraded lighting.
Plans are being discussed for a possible final round of games later this year, potentially bringing teams from Broome and Fitzroy Crossing to Derby for a showcase under the new lights.
The proposed event is yet to be confirmed, including a date, but the club says updates will be shared through its Facebook page as details become available.
For a club continuing to grow, Sunday’s 4-1 victory was more than just a win, it was a milestone for Derby soccer and a sign of bigger things to come.
